'''Din''' was a [[Star/Legends|star]] that at one point existed in the [[Din system]].<ref name="Endor" /> The [[Star system/Legends|system]] lay within the [[Outer Moddell systems]] area of<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]],<ref name="EAOC Din" /> one of the [[Sector/Legends|subsectors]] making up the [[Inner Zuma Region]]<ref name="TEA" /> within the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Zuma sector/Legends|Zuma sector]].<ref name="EAOC Din" /> The Din system was situated adjacent to the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Trindello-Endor Route]], which connected it to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor]] and [[Trindello system/Legends|Trindello systems]].<ref name="TEA" /> Din's name originated from the art and [[Music/Legends|songs]] of the [[Sanyassa system/Legends|Sanyassa system's]] [[Sanyassan/Legends|Sanyassan]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="Endor" />

Prior to its [[Din supernova|destruction]] in a [[Supernova/Legends|supernova]] in approximately [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], Din was [[Orbit/Legends|orbited]] by three [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]]&ndash;type [[Planet/Legends|planets]]. The supernova vaporized any inner planets Din may have had and boiled away the vast [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheres]] of the [[Gas/Legends|gas]] giants, leaving behind their exposed cores&mdash;one of which was a [[Diamond/Legends|diamond]] the size of a terrestrial world that had been formed by the intense pressure in the planet's atmosphere. The supernova left behind an energetic [[Din Pulsar/Legends|pulsar]] and an expanding [[Din Nebula/Legends|nebulosity]] of [[Color/Legends|red]] gases.<ref name="Endor" />

==Behind the scenes==
Din was first mentioned in the article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]," which was published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Endor" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Din system, and therefore its former star, in grid square H-16.<ref name="TEA" />
